title: Turf Wars of East New York

sentences.en: In the Bay Area, where I've lived for a couple of decades now,
sentences.zh: 在湾区，也就是我住了几十年的地方，

sentences.en: I've watched the front line of gentrification move further and further eaSt.
sentences.zh: 我眼看着士绅化的前线一步步向东推进。

sentences.en: This show is based in Oakland, as you probably know.
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，这个节目总部设在奥克兰。

sentences.en: And Oakland's quite big and heterogeneous, so you can never really talk about it as one thing.
sentences.zh: 奥克兰非常大且多元，所以你很难把它当作一个整体来谈论。

sentences.en: But in the last couple of years, rents have been going up,
sentences.zh: 但在过去几年里，租金一直在上涨，

sentences.en: and the fear is that rents will continue to go up to a point where only wealthy tech workers can afford it.
sentences.zh: 人们担心租金会持续上涨，直到只有富有的科技工作者才住得起。

sentences.en: This phenomenon is not unique to the Bay.
sentences.zh: 这种现象并非湾区独有。

sentences.en: East New York, a residential neighborhood on the eastern edge of Brooklyn, is going through this now too.
sentences.zh: 东纽约，这个位于布鲁克林东缘的住宅区，现在也正在经历这一切。

sentences.en: In the 1960s, East New York rapidly transformed from a mostly white working class neighborhood
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代，东纽约迅速从一个以白人为主的工人阶级社区，

sentences.en: to an underserved community of mostly black and brown New Yorkers, neglected by both society and policy.
sentences.zh: 转变成了一个以黑人和棕色人种为主的、被社会和政策双重忽视的边缘社区。

sentences.en: But now, as New York City rents skyrocket,
sentences.zh: 但现在，随着纽约市租金飞涨，

sentences.en: East New York is staring down a wave of gentrification that will forever change the character of this neighborhood
sentences.zh: 东纽约正面临着一波士绅化浪潮，这将永远改变这个社区的特质，

sentences.en: WNYC in New York and The Nation magazine have teamed up for an in-depth look at the gentrification of Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 纽约的WNYC电台和《国家》杂志联手对布鲁克林的士绅化进行了深入报道。

sentences.en: They call their series, There Goes the Neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 他们将这个系列节目命名为《社区不再》。

sentences.en: Today, we're showcasing an episode from this ongoing series that's really fantastic.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要展示这个正在进行的系列节目中非常精彩的一集。

sentences.en: It turns back the clock and looks at how this new, rather unlikely hotspot for gentrification
sentences.zh: 它回溯过去，审视这个全新的、相当出人意料的士绅化热点地区，

sentences.en: got to where it is today.
sentences.zh: 是如何走到今天这一步的。

sentences.en: This is episode three of There Goes the Neighborhood, Turf Wars, presented by Kai Wright of The Nation magazine.
sentences.zh: 这是《社区不再》的第三集《地盘之争》，由《国家》杂志的凯·赖特主持。

sentences.en: Are you going to sit down and take it to go?
sentences.zh: 你是要坐在这喝，还是带走？

sentences.en: The other day, I was walking in my neighborhood, and I saw a black elderly gentleman that I hadn't seen in a couple months,
sentences.zh: 那天我在社区散步，看到一位我几个月没见的黑人老先生，

sentences.en: and he literally, his eyes flew open, and he said,
sentences.zh: 他简直是瞪大了眼睛，说道：

sentences.en: This is some phenomenon that everybody sees, everybody feels, but somehow isn't in the center of the discussion where it needs to be.
sentences.zh: 这是一个每个人都能看到、每个人都能感受到的现象，但不知为何，它并没有处于讨论的核心位置，而它本应如此。

sentences.en: I am, of course, talking about gentrification.
sentences.zh: 我当然是在谈论士绅化。

sentences.en: When everybody gave up on the neighborhood, we didn't.
sentences.zh: 当所有人都放弃这个社区时，我们没有。

sentences.en: We worked it out, and we made it the better place that everybody wants to invest into now.
sentences.zh: 我们努力经营，把它变成了现在每个人都想投资的好地方。

sentences.en: We live on Barbie as family.
sentences.zh: 我们像家人一样住在芭比社区。

sentences.en: We're all there for each other.
They have also the political power to modify things.
sentences.zh: 他们也有政治权力来改变现状。

sentences.en: They can go and sit with commissioners and with high-ranked people and say, I need an extra block.
sentences.zh: 他们可以去和专员以及高层人士坐下来谈，说：“我需要多一个街区。”

sentences.en: I had a guy walking around my backyard.
sentences.zh: 有个家伙在我后院走来走去。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm looking to buy this property.
I said, Who are you looking to buy the property for?
sentences.zh: 我说：“你想替谁买这处房产？”

sentences.en: He says, Oh, dude, it's listed in foreclosure.
sentences.zh: 他说：“噢，伙计，这房子在法拍名单上。”

sentences.en: I said, Listen, dude, you're confused.
sentences.zh: 我说：“听着，伙计，你搞错了。”

sentences.en: All I see is overpopulating the city with others.
sentences.zh: 我只看到城市里挤满了外来人口。

sentences.en: The only ones that can afford this rent is people that's not from New York.
sentences.zh: 唯一付得起这租金的，都是些不是纽约本地的人。

sentences.en: Okay, and my income doesn't even give enough for a room in East New York.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的收入甚至在东纽约连个房间都租不起。

sentences.en: So how the hell is it going to give me for an apartment?
sentences.zh: 那它怎么可能让我租得起一套公寓呢？

sentences.en: I'm Kai Wright, and I'm an editor at The Nation magazine.
sentences.zh: 我是凯·赖特，我是《国家》杂志的编辑。

sentences.en: And my WNYC colleagues and I have been looking at this major demographic change that's happening all over Brooklyn now.
sentences.zh: 我和我的WNYC同事们一直在关注现在整个布鲁克林正在发生的这种重大人口结构变化。

sentences.en: Gentrification is one term that's applied to it.
sentences.zh: 士绅化是用来形容它的一种术语。

sentences.en: And a lot of people who are sick of hearing that term feel like, hey, this is just the law of supply and demand.
sentences.zh: 很多听腻了这个词的人觉得，嘿，这不过是供需法则罢了。

sentences.en: There's relatively cheap property available, and all things being equal, the people who can afford it grab it.
sentences.zh: 有相对便宜的房产，在其他条件相同的情况下，付得起钱的人就会抢购。

sentences.en: And the people who had it earlier, they reap the rewards.
sentences.zh: 而那些早先拥有它的人，则获得了回报。

sentences.en: But all things are not equal.
For decades, public policy stacked the deck of economic opportunity against Black people.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，公共政策在经济机会上一直对黑人不利。

sentences.en: Writer Ta-Nehisi Coates has spoken a lot about this fact lately in making his case for economic reparations.
sentences.zh: 作家塔-内西·科茨最近在为经济赔偿辩护时，多次谈到了这一事实。

sentences.en: He made the link to gentrification succinctly during a recent talk in Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 他在最近的一次布鲁克林演讲中，简洁地将此与士绅化联系了起来。

sentences.en: Neighborhoods change all the time in their makeup and their ethnic makeup.
sentences.zh: 社区的构成和族裔构成一直在变化。

sentences.en: The problem is Black people don't really have the same level of self-determination to decide whether they want to stay and whether they want to leave.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，黑人并没有同样的自决权来决定他们是想留下还是想离开。

sentences.en: When we built the middle class in this country, we made decisions about who was going to benefit.
sentences.zh: 当我们在这个国家建立中产阶级时，我们决定了谁将从中受益。

sentences.en: And we decided Black people weren't a part of that.
sentences.zh: 而我们决定了黑人不属于其中。

sentences.en: When we get to the point of talking about gentrification, you got to dig deep.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论士绅化时，你必须深入挖掘。

sentences.en: You got to go further back.
So today we take a long look back at East New York, the Brooklyn neighborhood that, as we started exploring last time, is now standing right in the path of gentrification.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我们深入回顾一下东纽约，正如我们上次开始探索的那样，这个布鲁克林社区现在正处于士绅化的道路上。

sentences.en: The first developer to set his sights on East New York was Colonel John Pitkin, way back in 1835.
sentences.zh: 第一个将目光投向东纽约的开发商是约翰·皮特金上校，早在1835年。

sentences.en: His family got rich on cotton and slaves, but went broke in the cotton crash of 1837.
sentences.zh: 他的家族靠棉花和奴隶发了财，但在1837年的棉花崩盘中破产了。

sentences.en: It was a lot like 2008, but back then the bubble was cotton, not subprime mortgages.
sentences.zh: 这和2008年很像，但那时泡沫是棉花，而不是次级抵押贷款。

sentences.en: Anyway, Pitkin lost his shirt in the crash, but not before launching this neighborhood into existence.
sentences.zh: 总之，皮特金在崩盘中输得精光，但在那之前，他已经让这个社区诞生了。

sentences.en: He bought up a bunch of farmland, built a shoe factory, and called it East New York.
sentences.zh: 他买下了一大片农田，建了一家鞋厂，并把它命名为东纽约。

sentences.en: Brooklyn's famous Pitkin Avenue still bears his name.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克林著名的皮特金大道至今仍以他的名字命名。

sentences.en: The Long Island Railroad came about a year later, and with it, factories to process foods from Long Island's farMs.
sentences.zh: 长岛铁路大约一年后开通，随之而来的是加工长岛农场食品的工厂。

sentences.en: The low-rise housing that still defines the area's skyline came next.
sentences.zh: 至今仍定义该地区天际线的低层住宅紧随其后。

sentences.en: Then more rail lines, connecting the area to Manhattan and the rest of Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 然后是更多的铁路线，将该地区与曼哈顿和布鲁克林的其他地方连接起来。

sentences.en: And it just kept growing, all the way through the middle of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 它就这样一直发展，贯穿了整个20世纪中叶。

sentences.en: East New York became a thriving suburb for the European immigrants who worked in all those factories.
sentences.zh: 东纽约成为了在那些工厂工作的欧洲移民的繁荣郊区。

sentences.en: Germans, and then Italians, and eventually Jewish families came here to feel, well, successful and American.
sentences.zh: 德国人，然后是意大利人，最后是犹太家庭来到这里，感受那种成功和美国梦。

sentences.en: It was sort of the suburbs in the city.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上是城市里的郊区。

sentences.en: It was a place where people strived to go.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人们努力向往的地方。

sentences.en: That's Ron Schiffman, a community organizer and urban planner who's been fighting the development wars in Brooklyn since the 60s.
sentences.zh: 那是罗恩·希夫曼，一位自60年代以来就一直在布鲁克林参与开发战争的社区组织者和城市规划师。

sentences.en: He grew up in Westchester, but spent a lot of time in East New York as a high school kid in the 50s.
sentences.zh: 他在威彻斯特长大，但在50年代读高中时，经常去东纽约。

sentences.en: My first girlfriend, actually, was in East New York.
sentences.zh: 其实，我的初恋女友就在东纽约。

sentences.en: I used to travel from lower Westchester County to meet her at the...
sentences.zh: 我过去常从下威彻斯特县赶去见她，在……

sentences.en: You must have been in love.
sentences.zh: 你当时一定坠入爱河了。

sentences.en: She was the daughter of a judge, lived in East New York.
sentences.zh: 她是法官的女儿，住在东纽约。

sentences.en: He paints an almost Norman Rockwell portrait of the place.
sentences.zh: 他描绘了一幅几乎像诺曼·洛克威尔画作般的社区肖像。

sentences.en: It was attached housing, but everybody had their own porch, and it was a middle-income, upper-middle-income community in many ways, or aspiring community.
sentences.zh: 那是联排住宅，但每个人都有自己的门廊，在很多方面，这是一个中等收入、中上收入的社区，或者说是一个有抱负的社区。

sentences.en: It was not what we think of today.
sentences.zh: 它不是我们今天所想的那样。

sentences.en: And then, all of a sudden, it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 然后，突然之间，它就不再是了。

sentences.en: Over the course of just four or five years, the neighborhood changed dramatically, from middle class to poor, from largely white to nearly all black.
sentences.zh: 在短短四五年间，这个社区发生了巨大的变化，从中产阶级变成了贫困，从以白人为主变成了几乎全是黑人。

sentences.en: In 1960, East New York was 85% white.
By 1966, it was 80% black and Puerto Rican.
sentences.zh: 到1966年，80%是黑人和波多黎各人。

sentences.en: What created such a stark change?
sentences.zh: 是什么造成了如此剧烈的变化？

sentences.en: A lot happened really fast, but there was a key moment.
sentences.zh: 很多事情发生得很快，但有一个关键时刻。

sentences.en: It happened on a hot summer night on July 21st, 1966.
sentences.zh: 它发生在1966年7月21日一个炎热的夏夜。

sentences.en: That's the day an 11-year-old black boy was shot.
sentences.zh: 那天，一名11岁的黑人男孩被枪杀。
吉姆·奥格雷迪带来了报道。

sentences.en: Here's a little hint that East New York was primed for racial tension in the summer of 1966.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个小线索，说明东纽约在1966年夏天已经处于种族紧张的边缘。

sentences.en: Some of its citizens got together and started a little self-help group called SPONGE, S-P-O-N-G-E, the Society for the Prevention of Negroes Getting Everything.
sentences.zh: 它的一些市民聚在一起，成立了一个名为SPONGE的小型自助组织，S-P-O-N-G-E，即“防止黑人得到一切协会”。

sentences.en: Of course, the group was whites only.
sentences.zh: 当然，该组织只招收白人。

sentences.en: Its members part of the 20% of the neighborhood that hadn't become black or Puerto Rican.
sentences.zh: 其成员属于社区中那20%尚未变成黑人或波多黎各人的群体。

sentences.en: A neighborhood that, as Kai said, ethnic whites had dominated demographically, economically, culturally, until as recently as five years before.
sentences.zh: 正如凯所说，这个社区直到五年前，在人口、经济和文化上一直由族裔白人所主导。

sentences.en: Anthony Momino was a teenager when the changes came down.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·莫米诺在这些变化发生时还是个少年。

sentences.en: He was born in Tunisia, but he's Italian.
sentences.zh: 他出生在突尼斯，但他是意大利人。

sentences.en: A lot of the whites in East New York were Italian.
sentences.zh: 东纽约的很多白人都是意大利人。

sentences.en: I remember where I lived, and it was mostly all white kids.
sentences.zh: 我记得我住的地方，几乎全是白人孩子。

sentences.en: Anybody crossed Euclid Avenue, black kid would cross there.
sentences.zh: 任何人穿过欧几里得大道，黑人孩子就会穿过那里。

sentences.en: They would chase them back there.
In the beginning, it was sort of like playing chicken.
sentences.zh: 起初，这有点像是在玩胆小鬼游戏。

sentences.en: The thing was, with them, it was a game.
sentences.zh: 问题是，对他们来说，这只是一场游戏。

sentences.en: So, you know, and the black kids used to come, I think, for the same reason, you know, let's get the white kids to chase us.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我想黑人孩子过来也是出于同样的原因，你知道，让我们去逗白人孩子来追我们。

sentences.en: Think about how disorienting it was to be in East New York in the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 想想看，在20世纪60年代初身处东纽约是多么令人困惑。

sentences.en: If you're white, you've seen your tight ethnic enclave flooded with newcomers.
sentences.zh: 如果你是白人，你眼看着自己紧密的族裔聚居区被新来者淹没。

sentences.en: If you're black or Puerto Rican, you're moving in for the affordable rents or the American dream of homeownership.
sentences.zh: 如果你是黑人或波多黎各人，你是为了负担得起的租金或拥有住房的美国梦而搬进来的。

sentences.en: You might have also migrated from the South to find a job and escape segregation.
sentences.zh: 你可能也是从南方迁移过来寻找工作并逃避种族隔离。

sentences.en: But now these cranky old timers are telling you, this ain't your place.
sentences.zh: 但现在这些脾气暴躁的老人们在告诉你，这不是你的地盘。

sentences.en: And you're probably thinking, dude, if this neighborhood is so wonderful,
sentences.zh: 你可能在想，伙计，如果这个社区这么好，

sentences.en: why did all the white folks, all at once, like a herd of antelope, move to Long Island?
sentences.zh: 为什么所有的白人，一下子就像一群羚羊一样，搬到了长岛？

sentences.en: I used to deliver the Brooklyn Eagle.
sentences.zh: 我过去常送《布鲁克林鹰报》。

sentences.en: And when I used to get to Broadway, I see one side of the street was black and the other side of the street was white.
sentences.zh: 当我走到百老汇时，我看到街道的一边是黑人，另一边是白人。

sentences.en: Then when I was in junior high, we got two black girls in there, and that was a big thing going on, you know.
sentences.zh: 后来我上初中时，班里来了两个黑人女孩，那可是件大事，你知道。

sentences.en: Then I had a friend of mine live across the street, went down to Alabama, and he got beat up for the simple reason.
sentences.zh: 后来我有个朋友住在街对面，去了阿拉巴马州，他因为一个简单的原因被打了。

sentences.en: He got up and gave a black woman a seat.
sentences.zh: 他站起来给一位黑人妇女让座。

sentences.en: And when he came back to Brooklyn, he had two black guys.
sentences.zh: 当他回到布鲁克林时，他带了两个黑人朋友。

sentences.en: So yeah, race relations in the South were obviously not good.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，南方的种族关系显然不好。

sentences.en: But in 1965, America was reminded in a big way, they're not good anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但在1965年，美国以一种巨大的方式被提醒，无论在哪里，种族关系都不好。

sentences.en: This is a network news report from the time.
sentences.zh: 这是一份当时的网络新闻报道。

sentences.en: The bloodiest riot in 40 years of America's troubled racial history begins.
sentences.zh: 美国动荡的种族史上40年来最血腥的骚乱开始了。

sentences.en: Los Angeles, California, the district called Watts.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州洛杉矶，被称为瓦茨的地区。

sentences.en: $40 million worth of property is destroyed.
sentences.zh: 价值4000万美元的财产被毁。

sentences.en: The American Negro, the invisible man, breaks out in a scream.
sentences.zh: 美国黑人，这个隐形人，爆发出一声尖叫。

sentences.en: Know me for what I am.
Look at me if you can.
So now it's a year after images of L.A.
sentences.zh: 现在距离洛杉矶燃烧的画面

sentences.en: burning have lit up American TV screens.
sentences.zh: 点亮美国电视屏幕已经过去一年了。

sentences.en: It's the start of the summer of 1966, and every major city is wondering,
sentences.zh: 那是1966年夏天的开始，每个大城市都在担心：

sentences.en: could the Watts riot happen here?
sentences.zh: 瓦茨骚乱会在这里发生吗？

sentences.en: New York's new mayor, John Lindsay, is fixated on preventing it.
sentences.zh: 纽约新任市长约翰·林赛一心想要阻止它发生。

sentences.en: Lindsay has been gathering a national reputation for walking the streets of New York at night
sentences.zh: 林赛因在夜间不带安保人员步行穿过纽约街道而闻名全国，

sentences.en: without a security detail, mostly in poor neighborhoods, as a gesture of concern.
sentences.zh: 他主要是在贫困社区这样做，以示关心。

sentences.en: Here's how he describes the tension in places like East New York.
sentences.zh: 以下是他对东纽约等地紧张局势的描述。

sentences.en: City governments have been largely absent from the ghettos.
sentences.zh: 市政府在贫民窟中几乎是缺位的。

sentences.en: Their chief presence usually has taken the form of a policeman.
sentences.zh: 他们主要的存在形式通常是一名警察。

sentences.en: And it has been his unhappy lot to be the lone representative of the man,
sentences.zh: 而他不幸的命运就是成为那个“白人”的唯一代表，

sentences.en: Whitey, and by extension, the entire public and private establishment.
sentences.zh: 也就是白人，进而代表了整个公共和私人体制。

sentences.en: Lindsay's chief of staff was Jay Kriegel, who was 26 at the time.
sentences.zh: 林赛的幕僚长是杰伊·克里格尔，当时他才26岁。

sentences.en: Today, he's a white-haired executive with the real estate giant Related Companies.
sentences.zh: 如今，他是一位白发苍苍的高管，就职于房地产巨头瑞联集团。

sentences.en: His office has a powerbroker's view of Columbus Circle, where he and I talked.
